info.name: SpendWise API
info.description:
Every endpoint of the SpendWise backend.

First use: import this collection and the SpendWise Local environment, run Auth > Login (demo@spendwise.app / Demo@2026 after `npm run seed`), then try any folder. Requests that create things save their id into a variable so Update and Delete work straight away.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Register, sign in and manage your account. Sign in (or register) first: its test script stores the token for every other request.

request.description: Password must be 8 to 72 characters with a letter and a number.
Repeated wrong passwords trigger a progressive lockout (30 s, 1 min, 5 min, 15 min, then 1 hour). The reply then has status 429, a Retry-After header and retryAfter in the body.
Only allowed before the first transaction exists.
Signs out every other device and returns a fresh token for this one.
Always answers the same way, whether or not the email has an account. The link is emailed, or printed in the server console when no email server is configured.
Paste the 64-character token from the reset link into the resetToken variable. Each link works once and expires after 30 minutes.
PERMANENT. Deletes the account and every record it owns.

item.name: Transactions
item.description: Income and expenses: full CRUD plus search, pagination, bulk actions and export.

request.description: Optional filters: type, category, search, month, year, date (YYYY-MM-DD). Returns transactions, totals for the whole filtered set, and pagination.
Up to 5,000 rows. The reply says truncated: true when the cap cut it off.
The same type, title and amount within a day of an existing entry returns 409 POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE. Repeat the request with ?force=true to add it anyway.
Each budget includes how much has been spent so far.
A budget for a category and month that already exists is updated instead.
Uses an atomic $inc, so simultaneous deposits cannot overwrite each other.

item.name: Bills
item.description: Spending that records itself every month on a set day.

request.description: Reading this also records any bill that has become due this month (once each, even if requests overlap).
Reading this also records any monthly income whose pay day has arrived.
If this month's pay day has already passed, recordThisMonth says whether the money has arrived (true records it now, false waits for next month).
Applies from the date given. Months already recorded are never rewritten.
Past income stays in the history but is unlinked from the source.

item.name: Categories
item.description: Your own spending and income categories.

request.description: Names must be unique and cannot reuse a built-in name. Up to 40 per account.
Renaming updates every transaction, budget, bill and income source that used the old name. The type cannot change.
If the category is in use, reassignTo says where its entries move to. Its budgets are removed.
